examples.solution_text:
Raise every factor inside the brackets, including the coefficient.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}(4x^{3}y^{2})^{2}\\&=4^{2}x^{3\times2}y^{2\times2}\\&=16x^{6}y^{4}\end{aligned}$

The negative coefficient is inside the brackets, so it is cubed too.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}(-4p^{2})^{3}\\&=(-4)^{3}p^{2\times3}\\&=-64p^{6}\end{aligned}$

An outside minus sign is not squared.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}-(2m)^{2}\\&=-\left(2^{2}m^{2}\right)\\&=-4m^{2}\end{aligned}$
An inside minus sign belongs to the coefficient being squared.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}(-2m)^{2}\\&=(-2)^{2}m^{2}\\&=4m^{2}\end{aligned}$

The outside factor $5$ stays unchanged; the inside coefficient $2$ is squared.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}5(2a^{3}b)^{2}\\&=5\times2^{2}a^{3\times2}b^{2}\\&=20a^{6}b^{2}\end{aligned}$

Square every factor in both the numerator and the denominator.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\left(\frac{4x^{3}}{3y^{2}}\right)^{2}\\&=\frac{4^{2}x^{3\times2}}{3^{2}y^{2\times2}}\\&=\frac{16x^{6}}{9y^{4}}\end{aligned}$

The outside factor $2$ is not cubed.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}2\left(\frac{p^{2}}{3q}\right)^{3}\\&=2\times\frac{p^{2\times3}}{3^{3}q^{3}}\\&=\frac{2p^{6}}{27q^{3}}\end{aligned}$

Expand the bracket power first, then divide the coefficients and subtract indices for each variable.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac{(2xy^{2})^{3}}{4x^{2}y}\\&=\frac{2^{3}x^{3}y^{2\times3}}{4x^{2}y}\\&=\frac{8x^{3}y^{6}}{4x^{2}y}\\&=2xy^{5}\end{aligned}$

Expand each bracket power, then multiply the coefficients and add the indices on $a$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}(3a^{2})^{2}\times(2a)^{3}\\&=3^{2}a^{4}\times2^{3}a^{3}\\&=9a^{4}\times8a^{3}\\&=72a^{7}\end{aligned}$

Expand the bracket power, then multiply by the reciprocal of the divisor.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac{w^{7}}{8}\div\left(\frac{w}{4}\right)^{2}\\&=\frac{w^{7}}{8}\div\frac{w^{2}}{16}\\&=\frac{w^{7}}{8}\times\frac{16}{w^{2}}\\&=2w^{5}\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: The equality $(10y^{n})^{m}=10\,000y^{28}$ is an identity in $y$, where $n$ and $m$ are positive whole numbers. Find $n$ and $m$.
examples.solution_text:
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}(10y^{n})^{m}\\&=10^{m}y^{nm}\end{aligned}$
Match the numerical factors: $10^{m}=10\,000=10^{4}$, so $m=4$.
Match the indices on $y$:
$\begin{aligned}4n&=28\\n&=7\end{aligned}$

examples.derivation: The outside minus gives -(2²m²) = -4m²; squaring the inside coefficient gives (-2)²m² = 4m².
Keep 5 outside the square: 5 × 2² × a⁶ × b² = 20a⁶b².
The squared numerator is 16x⁶ and the squared denominator is 9y⁴, giving 16x⁶/(9y⁴).
The powered numerator is 8x³y⁶. Dividing by 4x²y gives (8/4)x^(3-2)y^(6-1) = 2xy⁵.
The bracket powers give 9a⁴ and 8a³. Their product is 72a⁷.
The divisor becomes w²/16. Multiplication by 16/w² gives (16/8)w^(7-2) = 2w⁵.
Expansion gives 10^m y^(nm). Matching 10,000 = 10⁴ gives m = 4; matching nm = 28 gives n = 7.
